Gemini co-founder Tyler Winklevoss believes that the current mood surrounding Zcash ($ZEC) is comparable to crypto sentiment in 2019.

This comes after the privacy-focused cryptocurrency became the talk of the town because of its blistering rally.

Bitcoin entered 2019 in an unusually difficult position. The cryptocurrency had just gone through the brutal 2018 bear market following the speculative frenzy of 2017. Prices were depressed while retail enthusiasm had evaporated.
According to CoinGecko's retrospective data, Bitcoin was worth roughly $3,693 on Jan. 1, 2019. It went on to rally to around $13,000 by late June before retracing some of that increase, eventually entering 2020 around $7,195.

Despite the volatility, the people paying close attention to Bitcoin were discussing institutional infrastructure, custody, and so on. The same applies to the broader industry.

The suggestion appears to be that Zcash currently has a similar feeling of enthusiasm.

Real-time news, insights, prices, trending stories, and expert analysis - all in one place.IPO Out in the Cold? Robot Bosses Burn Incense, Kowtow, and Dig Up Old ScoresThe article examines the cooling IPO prospects for China's embodied AI robotics companies. After Unitree's listing in August 2026, the anticipated wave of robot IPOs failed to materialize. Zhizhen Robot reportedly abandoned its plan to list within the year, pursuing instead a new funding round of 1-1.5 billion yuan at a ~50 billion yuan valuation, which would trigger a 120-day waiting period before listing. Other companies like Galbot, X Square Robot, and LimX Dynamics have also seen their timelines slip.

The slowdown is driven by regulatory scrutiny. Authorities increasingly focus on whether companies can demonstrate verifiable technological leadership and real commercial potential. Capital markets struggle to assess how much value created by better models actually stays on the company's books, given costs for compute, data processing, deployment, and human review. Analysts caution that primary-market valuations may not hold in secondary markets, especially when revenue projections rely on unproven pilots.

The article details the legal and financial tangles that trip up IPO applicants, often rooted in early-stage financing: shareholding proxies, capital contribution flaws, offshore trust structures, shareholder penetration checks, and investor special rights like redemption and anti-dilution clauses. Employee equity incentives at high valuations create heavy repurchase burdens when staff depart. Intellectual property disputes arise when engineers move between companies or universities, requiring verification of invention ownership. Surprise whistleblower reports and regulatory on-site inspections are described as swords hanging over every applicant.

Crypto PAC Spending Against Sherrod Brown Passes $52 Million In Ohio | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto NewsMarket AnalysisCrypto PAC Spending Against Sh...Crypto PAC Spending Against Sherrod Brown Passes $52 Million In OhiobitcoinistPublished on 2026-10-18Last updated on 2026-10-18AbstractCrypto-aligned political committees have spent over $52 million in Ohio against former Senator Sherrod Brown's bid to return to Congress, marking one of the clearest examples of the industry's willingness to spend heavily on a single Senate seat. Federal Election Commission filings show Defend American Jobs, an affiliate of the Fairshake network, reported about $46.67 million in expenditures opposing Democrat Sherrod Brown and supporting Republican incumbent Jon Husted. A separate committee, the Digital Freedom Fund, reported approximately $5.94 million, bringing the combined total to nearly $52.61 million. Brown is a former US senator seeking to return to the chamber, not the sitting incumbent, and the spending aims to keep the seat with Husted in the November midterm election. Fairshake and related groups have received financial support from major crypto companies including Coinbase and Ripple, reflecting the industry's interest in who controls the committee agenda and how future digital-asset rules are negotiated in Washington. The Ohio total shows how quickly campaign commitments can grow, as Defend American Jobs' reported amount is well above the $30 million previously earmarked for the race. These figures represent political spending, not money contributed directly to a candidate's official campaign account. bonuses.requirements: Italy Dismantles Mafia-Linked Underground Bank, Involved in $76.29 Million Money Laundering with CryptocurrencyHomeFeedNewsItaly Dismantles Mafia-Linked Underground Bank, Involved in $76.29 Million Money Laundering with CryptocurrencyItaly Dismantles Mafia-Linked Underground Bank, Involved in $76.29 Million Money Laundering with Cryptocurrency10/24 08:10On Wednesday, October 21, the Italian Financial Police (Guardia di Finanza) in Milan, in collaboration with the Milan Anti-Mafia District Prosecutor's Office (DDA), dismantled a network of underground banks linked to the Mafia, arresting 30 individuals with over 350 police officers involved in the operation. This network was based in a car rental company in Pero, near Milan, and involved members of the 'Ndrangheta family from Crotone and the Casalesi family. They issued over 110 million euros (approximately 123.45 million dollars) in false invoices to businesses in logistics and construction sectors, helping them evade taxes, and then returned the funds in cash while charging a fee, with the cash sourced from tax evasion and drug trafficking. Funds from shell company accounts were first transferred to lenders in Luxembourg, Lithuania, and Germany, and then flowed into digital wallets controlled by the organization through cryptocurrency exchanges, involving approximately 68 million euros (about 76.29 million dollars) in foreign exchange. Authorities plan to confiscate assets worth 21 million euros (approximately 23.56 million dollars); Spanish police are executing a European arrest warrant, and Swiss authorities are pursuing another suspect.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。Related ArticlesCross River Bank Adds Ripple’s RLUSD To Its Payment InfrastructureSweden’s Riksbank Urges Lawmakers to Prepare for Digital KronaQivalis receives EMI authorization from Dutch central bank for euro stablecoinAll Comments0LatestHotL

He said owners will be able to ask the Roadster to perform any of the tricks shown at its presentation by itself. Musk also mentioned that a wild loop track, even crazier than Hot Wheels, will be built at Tesla's Texas headquarters for testing the Roadster. He explained that the Roadster is based on a by-wire control system, where the steering wheel and pedals send signals to an onboard computer instead of using mechanical linkages. The computer then uses sensor data to control electric motors that steer, brake, and accelerate the car. You just need to ask, and the car will repeat any of the tricks shown at the presentation without the driver's participation.
He wrote: "You will be able to ask the Roadster to perform any of the shown tricks on its own, because it will possess consciousness.
